label: Guzerá

names.text: Wikipedia's Guzerat cattle article (opened): alternative names Azulego, Kankrej and Guzerat. It says the name is a Portuguese spelling of Gujarat.

about.text: Brazil's zebu breed, descended from Kankrej bulls brought from Gujarat in India from about 1870 and crossed with local Crioulo cows. It is kept for beef and dual-purpose use, and its herdbook has a dual-purpose dairy line, the Guzerá Leiteiro.

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened): Kankrej bulls from Gujarat imported from about 1870 and crossed with Crioulo cows in Minas Gerais; herdbook lists a beef type, the dual-purpose Guzerá Leiteiro and a polled variant; purposes listed as meat and dual-purpose. The Frontiers 2022 paper (found in WebSearch text, not opened, no URL kept) says the breed serves beef, milk or dual-purpose systems.

origin.place: Minas Gerais, Brazil, from Kankrej cattle of Gujarat, India, imported in the late 19th century

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened): Kankrej bulls from Gujarat imported from about 1870 into the Cerrado of Minas Gerais and crossed with local Crioulo cows; Guzerá spread to the Northeast and to several states. The 1870 to 1900 range also reflects the Frontiers 2022 paper (found in WebSearch text, not opened), which dates the introduction of Indian breeds to the end of the 19th century.

Wikipedia (opened): about 92,000 head registered in 2010, roughly 3.5% of Brazil's indicine cattle, with about 17,500 new registrations that year. These are herdbook registrations, not a total population.
Wikipedia (opened): listed as meat and dual-purpose. Frontiers in Genetics 2022 (WebSearch text, not opened): serves beef, milk or dual-purpose systems, with dual-purpose as the selection goal.

Wikipedia (opened) cites FAO (2007) listing the breed as not at risk and says DAD-IS (2025) also lists it as not at risk. DAD-IS itself was not opened; the 2025 year and the status are as Wikipedia gives them.

facts.v: In 7,859 Guzerá lactation records from Brazilian herds, 1984 to 1996, mean milk yield was 8.60 ± 2.82 kg per day and mean lactation length 290.64 ± 34.17 days.

sources.text: Found in WebSearch text, not opened: 7,859 Guzerá lactation records from Brazilian herds, 1984 to 1996, with mean milk yield 8.60 ± 2.82 kg per day and mean lactation length 290.64 ± 34.17 days. Peak yield was about 9.1 kg per day at the fifth calving.

facts.v: The herdbook distinguishes a beef type, a dual-purpose meat-and-dairy line (Guzerá Leiteiro) and a polled variant (Guzerá Mocho).

sources.text: Wikipedia (opened). The article gives no production figures for the dairy line.

gaps: The 2022 herdbook total is given only as 'just under 40000' on Wikipedia, with no exact count, so it is not entered. No per-lactation or per-year milk yield was found for the breed. No production figures were found for the Guzerá Leiteiro dairy line. Composition (fat, protein, lactose, solids) was not found.
